title: Managing the Spiders
summary: Matassa recorded and managed the Spiders, switching them from gospel to R&B, buying uniforms and a station wagon and sending Phyllis Boone on the road, without seeking profit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah. So, I always... I'm always kind of amazed why we didn't have more local entrepreneurship.
Even I didn't.
You didn't even...
A couple of times I recorded people, but I recorded them because I thought they needed to be recorded. I mean, you know, like the Spiders, for instance.
Mm-hmm.
You know, I did everything for the Spiders. I became their manager.
Mm-hmm.

Not because I was going to make a fortune out of it, but because I saw... They had a potential, you know. They were great singers, a great group, and they were amenable to switching from gospel to rhythm and blues, you know.
Is that when you first heard them, they were doing gospel?
Yeah.
Mm-hmm. Yeah.
And, gee, I bought them uniforms. I bought them a station wagon. You know, I hired somebody to go on the road with them.
Right.
A butch gal named Phyllis Boone. Mm-hmm.
I don't know if you ever met her. Right. Didn't she work for you at one time?
Yeah, she worked for me, yeah.
She was a secretary of some time?
Okay. And I sent her out on the road. There. Everything. I tried to.
But what became of your managerial instincts? I mean, I know the Spiders went on...

I wasn't a manager to be a manager. Yeah. That's what was wrong. Right. It was what was missing. Right. I didn't understand that I should have been trying to make a lot of money, you know, to another failing time.
Right. Okay. I mean, I understand. I understand that mindset because I've been there a couple of times. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. You know, you get involved with people you like and they got some talent going for them and you call yourself out. Yeah, it's getting worse. It's better than that.
